Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She was only three years old and she loved playing with her friends.
One day Sarah went to the park with her friends. They were all very excited. As they played, Sarah saw two boys fighting. She frowned, she did not like fighting.
The other kids saw Sarah frowning and they all started saying, "Why are you frowning Sarah?"
Sarah replied, " I don't like it when boys fight."
Her friends agreed and they all decided to teach the two boys a different way to play without fighting.
After a while of playing, Sarah and her friends were very excited to see the two boys were now playing nicely together.
Sarah smiled and everyone was happy.

Once upon a time, a boy and his dad went for a walk. It was a sunny day and they wanted to explore. As they walked, they saw a hill.
"Let's go up there!" said the boy.
"Okay," said Dad.
So they started walking up the hill. It was open with lots of long grass, and the sun was shining brightly on them.
When they reached the top, they could see all the way to the horizon. It was so open! They looked all around, until the boy spotted something that made him smile.
"What is it?" asked Dad.
"A rabbit!" said the boy. He was teasing it by tickling its neck with a flower.
The rabbit didn't seem to mind. It hopped away and the boy laughed.
Dad and the boy looked around some more, enjoying the view from the top of the hill.
It was a perfect day!

One day, a little girl named Ella saw a pen on the ground. She could not resist picking it up and began to play with it. She pretended it was a magic wand and waved it around happily.
Suddenly, her brother Tom came up to her and snatched the pen from her hands. He laughed and said, "I'm going to keep this pen all to myself."
Ella was very angry and she said, "That's not fair at all! Give me the pen!"
Tom just shook his head and said, "No way. It's mine now."
Ella was so mad that she started to cry. Tom felt bad and said, "Come on, you know I'm just joking! Here you can have it back." He gave the pen back to Ella and they both laughed.
Tom had been a bit too selfish, but they both learned a valuable lesson. From then on, they shared everything they had and spread the joy of sharing to everyone around them.

Sam showed Tom how to tie his shoes. Tom tried and tried, but he could not do it. Then, a big, healthy dog came running over. The dog picked up Tom's shoe in its mouth. The dog was trying to help Tom tie his shoe!
Tom laughed and said, "Thank you, dog!" The dog helped Tom tie his shoes. Now, Tom could ride a bike with Sam. They had lots of fun at the park. The big, healthy dog went home with Tom and became his new best friend.

Sam wanted to soar. He was 3 years old and wanted to fly in the sky. He had no wings, but he still found a way. He grabbed his radio and put it outside on the roof. Then he laid down on the ground and held onto his radio. Suddenly, with a burst of energy, Sam was flying! He soared higher and higher, and he could not believe it! He was flying!
But then, Sam suddenly felt something was wrong. He was getting farther and farther away from his home. He started to feel troubled and scared, not sure how to get back. He looked up at the sky and saw a plane. He closed his eyes and wished he could be like the plane - flying back to his home.
Miraculously, his wish came true! With a little help from a magical wind, Sam zoomed back to his home. He was so excited! He thanked the wind and hugged his radio. From that day on, whenever Sam felt troubled, he would grab his radio and go outside. He knew he could always soar, with a little help from the wind.

One day, a nice boy named Tim saw a silver toy car in the shop. He really wanted it, so he asked his mom if he could have it. His mom said yes, and they bought the silver toy car. Tim was very happy.
Tim and his friend, Sam, went to the park to play with the silver toy car. They took turns making the car rush fast on the ground. They had so much fun, and the car went very, very fast.
But then, something unexpected happened. The silver toy car rushed too fast and went into the street. A big truck came and hit the toy car. The silver toy car broke into many small pieces. Tim and Sam were very sad, and they learned to be more careful when playing with their toys.

Lily and Max are playing with their toys in the living room. Lily has a doll and Max has a truck. They are having fun making noises and moving their toys around.
"Vroom, vroom, my truck is fast and strong!" Max says.
"Look, my doll can dance and sing!" Lily says.
They are both happy and lively.
Then, Max sees Lily's doll and wants to play with it. He puts his truck down and reaches for the doll.
"Hey, give me that!" he says.
"No, this is my doll!" Lily says. She pulls the doll away from Max.
"Please, let me have it for a little while!" Max says.
"No, you have your truck!" Lily says. She refuses to share her doll with Max.
Max gets angry and grabs his truck. He tries to hit Lily's doll with his truck.
"Stop it, that's not nice!" Lily says. She cries and hugs her doll.
Their mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees Lily and Max fighting over their toys.
"What's going on here?" she asks.
"Lily won't share her doll with me!" Max says.
"Max tried to hit my doll with his truck!" Lily says.
Mom shakes her head and sighs. She picks up Max and Lily and sits them on the couch.
"Listen, you two. You have to learn to share and be kind to each other. You have plenty of toys to play with. You don't need to fight over one. How would you feel if someone took your toy away or hit it with another toy?" she says.
Lily and Max look at each other and feel sorry. They realize they were wrong and mean.
"I'm sorry, Lily. I shouldn't have tried to take your doll or hit it with my truck." Max says.
"I'm sorry, Max. I shouldn't have refused to share my doll with you." Lily says.
They hug each other and say they are sorry.
Mom smiles and kisses them both.
"That's better. Now, why don't you play nicely together? You can take turns with your toys or find something else to do. How about we read a book or draw a picture?" she says.
Lily and Max nod and agree. They put their toys away and follow Mom to the bookshelf. They are happy and lively again.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the garden. There is a big hedge in the garden. The hedge has many leaves and flowers. Sara and Ben like to hide behind the hedge and pretend they are animals.
One day, Sara and Ben are playing behind the hedge. Sara says, "I am a lion. I roar and run fast. What are you, Ben?"
Ben says, "I am a bird. I sing and fly high. Watch me, Sara!"
Ben tries to jump over the hedge, but he is not ready. He falls on the other side of the hedge. Sara hears a thud and a cry.
"Ben, are you okay?" Sara asks. She runs to the hedge and looks over.

Sara says, "It's okay, Ben. You are brave. You tried to fly like a bird. But you need to be careful. The hedge is too high for you. Come, I will help you."
Sara helps Ben to stand up. She hugs him and says, "You are my friend. I like to play with you. Let's go to the house and get a band-aid and a new shirt. Then we can play again. Maybe we can be something else. What do you want to be, Ben?"
Ben smiles and says, "I want to be a hedge. I can be green and quiet and have many leaves and flowers. What do you want to be, Sara?"
Sara thinks and says, "I want to be a hedge too. We can be hedge friends. We can hide and pretend and have fun. Come on, Ben. Let's go and get ready to be hedges."

One day, Lily wants to watch a show about animals. She likes to see the lions and the monkeys. Max wants to watch a show about cars. He likes to see the fast and loud cars.
They both grab the remote and pull. They yell at each other.

Lily and Max nod. They feel sorry for fighting.

"Yes, you can. And can you give each other a hug?" Mom asks.
Lily and Max say sorry and hug each other. They feel better.

"That's very good. I'm proud of you. Now, do you want to watch something together?" Mom asks.
Lily and Max look at each other and nod.
"Can we watch a show about dinosaurs?" they ask.
Mom laughs and nods.
"Sure, you can. Dinosaurs are fun. But first, can you remind me what a dinosaur is?" Mom asks.
Lily and Max think hard and try to explain.
"A dinosaur is a big animal that lived a long time ago. Some have sharp teeth and some have long necks. Some are green and some are brown. They make loud noises like roar and stomp. They are not here anymore. They are gone." Lily and Max say.
Mom nods and smiles.
"That's very clear. You are very smart. Let's watch the show then." Mom says.
She turns on the television and finds a show about dinosaurs. Lily and Max watch with Mom and learn new things. They are happy and quiet. They do not fight anymore.

But, the missile was too big and heavy for Tom and Sam. They tried very hard, but they could not load the missile. The missile fell and broke. Tom and Sam were sad because they could not load the missile. The end.

Lily was a bird who loved to sing. She had a very pretty voice and a very fancy wing. She liked to show off her wing and her voice to the other birds. She did not care if they were busy or tired. She just wanted them to listen and admire her.
One day, she saw a big tree with many flowers. She flew there and saw many bees. She thought they would like her singing too. She started to perform her best song. She flapped her fancy wing and sang very loud.
But the bees did not like her singing. They were working hard to make honey. They did not want to hear a noisy bird. They got angry and buzzed at her. "Go away, go away, you are bothering us!" they said.
Lily did not listen. She thought they were jealous of her wing and her voice. She sang louder and louder. She did not see a big spider coming. The spider was hungry and saw a tasty bird. He spun a web and caught Lily in it.
Lily was scared and sorry. She could not sing or flap her wing. She wished she had been nicer to the other birds and the bees. She wished she had not been so proud and rude. She hoped someone would help her.
A little ant saw Lily in the web. He felt sorry for her. He knew she had a good voice and a fancy wing. He also knew she had a bad habit of showing off. He decided to help her. He bit the web and made a hole. He told Lily to be quiet and escape.
Lily was very grateful to the ant. She thanked him and flew away. She learned a lesson that day. She learned that being fancy and talented is not enough. She also needed to be humble and kind. She decided to be a better bird and a better friend.

Once upon a time there was a brave soldier who chose to stand guard in a field. The field was thick with tall grass and the soldier kept watch day and night.
One day the soldier noticed something strange - he didn't hear any birds. The soldier searched for the birds, but they seemed to have vanished. He even searched in the tall grass, but couldn't find any sign of them.
The soldier soon discovered why the birds had disappeared. A farmer had come to mow the tall grass, creating a huge cloud of dust. The birds had vanished to escape the dust.
The soldier wasn't happy about the farmer mowing the grass - he knew the birds needed it in order to hide and live. So he spoke to the farmer and taught him a lesson. He taught him to be more careful and to remember that it is important to look after nature.
After that the farmer understood the importance of taking care of the birds and so he only cut the grass in a way that allowed the birds to still live there.
The soldier felt very proud of his lesson - he had taught the farmer to not be careless and to remember that nature is precious.

Once, there lived a little girl called Anna. She was three and every day she used to play in her garden. She liked collecting things such as flowers, stones and pretty leaves.
One day, while Anna was in her garden, she saw an enormous bonfire nearby. She wanted to get closer to have a better look, but her mother shouted at her, ‘Anna, stay away from there! Don’t get too close or your shirt will burn.’
Anna thought about what her mother said and instead of getting closer to the bonfire, she went back to playing in her garden.
Later that evening, Anna’s father came running in the garden. ‘Anna, I saw in the road a group of older kids playing with a burning ball,’ he said. ‘One of them dropped it and when it rolled down the hill, it almost hit your shirt.’
At that moment, Anna remembered what her mother said about not getting too close to the bonfire. She realized that she may have lost her shirt if she had come near the big fire.
This story tells us that it is important to listen to the advice of our parents, because they often know what’s best for us.

Tom and Sue were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They were very happy.
"Look at our snowman! He is so big and nice!" Tom said.
"Yes, he is! But we have to go home soon. It is getting dark and cold." Sue said.
They said goodbye to their snowman and ran to their house. They had hot chocolate and cookies with their mom. They were very warm and cozy.
The next morning, they wanted to see their snowman again. But when they looked out the window, they saw something very sad. Their snowman was gone! There was only a pile of snow, a hat, a scarf and a carrot on the ground.
"What happened to our snowman?" Tom asked.
"He melted, Tom. The sun was too hot for him. He became water and then he became zero." Sue explained.
"Zero? What is zero?" Tom asked.
"Zero is nothing, Tom. Nothing at all." Sue said.
They felt very sad. They loved their snowman. They went outside to pick up his hat, his scarf and his carrot. They were very wet and filthy.
"Maybe we can make another snowman someday, Sue." Tom said.
"Maybe, Tom. But not today. Today we have to take a bath and clean our clothes." Sue said.
They went back to their house. They said goodbye to their snowman again. They hoped he was happy somewhere. They hoped he would come back someday.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big slide that looked fun. Ben wanted to go on the slide, but Lily was scared.
"Come on, Lily, it's not so high. I dare you to go on the slide with me," Ben said.
"No, Ben, I don't want to. It's too fast and too steep. I might fall and hurt myself," Lily said.
Ben was frustrated. He thought Lily was being silly. He wanted to show her that the slide was not scary at all. He had an idea.
"Look, Lily, I can make the slide even more fun. I can slide down holding this wire. It will make me go faster and smoother. Watch me," Ben said.
He grabbed a wire that was hanging from a nearby tree. He climbed up the ladder and sat on the slide. He held the wire with both hands and pushed himself down.
But Ben did not know that the wire was not strong enough to hold his weight. As he slid down, the wire snapped and he lost his balance. He tumbled down the slide and landed on the ground with a thud.
"Ow, ow, ow," Ben cried. He had scraped his knees and elbows and bumped his head.
Lily ran to him and helped him up. She was worried about him.
"Ben, are you okay? That was a bad idea. You should not play with wires. They can be dangerous. You could have hurt yourself more," Lily said.
Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He realized that Lily was right. He had been foolish and reckless. He hugged Lily and apologized.
"I'm sorry, Lily. You were smart and I was dumb. I should have listened to you. I won't dare you to do things that are scary or risky anymore. Can we still be friends?" Ben said.
Lily smiled and nodded. She forgave Ben and hugged him back.
"Of course we can, Ben. We are always friends. But next time, let's play something safer and nicer. How about the swings or the sandbox?" Lily said.
Ben agreed. He and Lily walked to the swings, holding hands. They forgot about the slide and the wire. They had fun together.

Once upon a time, in a hot summer day, a little girl named Sue played in her yard. She saw a dirty, little cat. The cat was sad and hungry. Sue wanted to help the cat.
Sue went to her mom and said, "Mom, can I give the cat some food?" Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful." Sue took some food and went back to the yard. She put the food on the ground and hid behind a tree to peek.
As Sue peeked, she saw the dirty cat eat the food. Then, something unexpected happened. The dirty cat changed into a beautiful, clean cat with shiny fur! The cat said, "Thank you, Sue, for helping me. I am a magic cat, and now I can help you too."
From that day on, Sue and the magic cat were the best of friends. They played together every summer day, and they were always happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy had a cat named Mr. Whiskers. They lived a happy life in a small house.
One day, Amy found a spicy pepper in the kitchen. She thought it would be fun to tease Mr. Whiskers with it. She waved the spicy pepper in front of Mr. Whiskers and said, "Look, Mr. Whiskers! Do you want to try this spicy thing?"
Mr. Whiskers sniffed the pepper and sneezed. Amy laughed and said, "I'm sorry, Mr. Whiskers. I didn't mean to make you sneeze." Mr. Whiskers looked at her and meowed, as if to say, "It's okay, Amy."
From that day on, Amy and Mr. Whiskers continued to have fun and play together. They learned not to tease each other with spicy things. And they lived a happy life, full of love and laughter.

In the x-ray room, Tim met a rude girl named Lily. She said, "I don't like x-rays, they're scary!" Tim told her, "My mom said if we pray, we won't be scared." Lily thought for a moment and said, "Okay, let's try it."
They prayed together, and something unexpected happened. The x-ray machine turned into a fun toy! Tim and Lily played with it and were not scared anymore. The doctor was surprised but happy to see them having fun. From that day on, Tim and Lily became best friends and always prayed together when they were scared.

Once upon a time, there was a fierce lion who lived in the forest. The lion was big and strong. He loved to wink at all the animals that he saw. One day, the lion met a small mouse. The mouse was very scared of the lion.
"Hello, little mouse," said the lion with a big wink. "Do not be scared of me. I love all the animals in the forest."
"But you are so fierce," said the mouse, still scared. "I am just a small mouse. What if you hurt me?"
The lion smiled and said, "I promise I will not hurt you. I just want to be your friend."
The mouse decided to trust the fierce lion and they became friends. They played together every day, and the lion always winked at the mouse. But one day, the lion was very hungry. He looked at the mouse and thought about eating him. The mouse saw the lion's face and knew something was wrong.
"Please, Mr. Lion, do not eat me," cried the mouse. But the lion was too hungry and did not listen. He ate the mouse, and the mouse was gone forever. The lion was very sad because he lost his friend, but it was too late.

He couldn't find the vegetable again, so he decided to go inside. Jack had a lot of fun kicking his vegetable. He couldn't wait to go back in the garden and find another hard vegetable!

Once upon a time, there was a big hairy dog named Ben. Ben loved to go on walks with his best friend, a little boy named Tim. One sunny day, they went to the park near the big blue sea.
At the park, they saw a small boat with a sail. The sail was red and white, just like a candy cane. Tim and Ben wanted to ride the boat, but they did not know how. A kind old man saw them and said, "I can teach you how to sail the boat, but you must always tell the truth."
Tim and Ben agreed, and they learned to sail the boat. They had so much fun on the water, going fast and slow. The wind blew the sail, and they felt happy and free. After their ride, the old man asked if they liked it. Tim said, "Yes, it was the best!" But Ben, the hairy dog, told a lie. He said, "No, it was not fun."
The old man knew Ben was lying. He told Ben that lying was not good. It could hurt people's feelings and make them sad. Ben felt bad for lying and said sorry to the old man and Tim. He promised to always tell the truth from that day on.
Tim and Ben learned a very important lesson that day. They learned that telling the truth is always the best thing to do. And they sailed the boat many more times, always remembering to be honest with each other and their friends.

Soon, the little fox was lost. He did not know where he was or how to go back. He was scared and hungry and tired. He saw a gray wolf, who had sharp teeth and yellow eyes. The wolf saw the little fox and wanted to eat him. He growled and ran after him.
The little fox ran as fast as he could, but the wolf was faster. He caught up with him and bit his tail. The little fox cried out in pain and fear. He wished he had listened to his mother and stayed in their den.
But then, he heard a loud roar. It was his father, who had heard his cry and came to help him. He was big and strong and brave. He fought the wolf and made him leave. He licked the little fox's wound and carried him back to their den.
The little fox was happy to see his mother and his brothers and sisters. He hugged them and thanked them for saving him. He learned his lesson. He never ran away from his den again. He always listened to his mother and father. He knew they loved him and wanted him to be safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to eat radish from the garden. One day, Remy found a big, yummy radish. It was the biggest radish he had ever seen! He was so happy and excited to eat it.
Remy started to eat the big radish, but he felt a sharp pain in his mouth. "Ouch!" he cried, and he felt dizzy. He didn't know what to do. Suddenly, a wise old turtle named Toby came by. He saw Remy in pain and asked, "What's wrong, little rabbit?"
Remy told Toby about the sharp pain and how dizzy he felt. Toby looked at the big radish and said, "You need to be careful, Remy. This radish is not good for you. It will make you feel bad." Remy listened to Toby and stopped eating the radish.
Remy learned that not everything that looks good is good for you. He thanked Toby for helping him and promised to be more careful next time. From that day on, Remy always asked for help when he was not sure about something. And he lived happily ever after.

"Dad, can I pet the cow?" she asks.
"Sure, Anna, but you have to be careful. Cows are very big and strong. They can kick or push you if they are scared or angry. Let me teach you how to pet a cow safely," dad says.
Dad shows Anna how to approach the cow slowly and gently. He tells her to talk to the cow in a soft voice and touch her on the neck or the back. He says to avoid the cow's head, horns, legs and tail. He says to always watch the cow's eyes and ears for signs of how she feels.
Anna follows dad's instructions and pets the cow. The cow makes a low moo and lets Anna stroke her fur. Anna feels happy and brave. She thinks the cow is nice and friendly.
"Good job, Anna. You are a fast learner. The cow likes you. Do you want to give her a name?" dad asks.
Anna thinks for a moment. She remembers the cow's big brown eyes and long lashes. She says, "I want to call her Lila. She is pretty like a flower."
Dad smiles and hugs Anna. He says, "That's a lovely name, Anna. Lila is lucky to have you as a friend."

Once upon a time there was a big, orange muscle. Everyone was amazed at how strong it was!
One day, the muscle went to the park. It saw its friend, a little mouse.
The mouse said, “Oh no! I’m stuck. Can you help me?”
The muscle said, “Yes! I have a plan. I will reverse and then I will be stronger. That will help us both!”
So the muscle reversed. It became stronger, and was able to pull the mouse from where it was stuck.
The mouse said, “Thank you! You are the strongest muscle I know!”
The muscle said, “You’re welcome! Now let’s go have some fun!”

"Don't be silly, Ben. It's just a spider. It won't hurt you. Watch this!" Mia said, and reached out to touch the spider gently.
But as soon as she touched it, the spider jumped on her hand and ran up her arm. Mia screamed and shook her arm, trying to get the spider off. Ben laughed and pointed at her.
"Haha, Mia, you're so funny! You're scared of a harmless spider! You're so embarrassed!" Ben said, still holding the flashlight.
Mia felt angry and sad. She didn't like Ben laughing at her. She didn't think it was funny. She grabbed the flashlight from Ben and turned it off.
"Hey, give that back! I can't see anything!" Ben said, feeling scared in the dark.

"I'm sorry, Mia. Ben was not nice to you. He shouldn't have laughed at you. He should have helped you. Maybe he was embarrassed too, because he was scared of the spider. "Thanks, Mia. I'm sorry I laughed at you. That was mean. I was scared of the spider too. I didn't mean to make you feel bad." Ben said, looking at Mia.
"It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. I was scared too. But you know, spiders are harmless. They don't want to hurt us. They just want to live in the garden. Maybe we can learn more about them and see how cool they are." Mia said, smiling.
"Really? Do you think so? Maybe you're right. Maybe we can be friends with the spiders. And with each other." Ben said, smiling back.

All the animals searched high and low for the pretty veil. At last, they found it in a bush. The little bird was so happy! She thanked the big lion and all the animals for their help.
The big lion and the little bird learned that helping each other is very important. They stayed friends forever, always ready to help one another. And every time the lion roared, it was a reminder that friends should always help each other.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old owl who lived in a big tree. He had a staff of little birds who helped him. They all worked together to keep the forest clean and safe.
One day, a small bird named Timmy was very tired. He said, "I want to quit. I don't want to help anymore." The wise owl asked, "Why do you want to quit, Timmy?" Timmy replied, "I am too small, and I can't do much." The wise owl said, "Remember, even small things can make a big difference."
The next day, a big storm came to the forest. Many leaves and branches fell on the ground. The wise owl and the staff of little birds started cleaning up. Timmy saw a small hole in the tree where water was coming in. He thought, "I can fix this!" He used his small body to block the hole and stop the water.
After the storm, the wise owl said, "Thank you, Timmy! You saved our home." Timmy was happy and didn't want to quit anymore. He learned that even small birds can do big things. The moral of the story is, "No matter how small you are, you can make a big difference."

Anna put a band-aid on Tim's leg. Tim felt better and started to clap his hands. He said, "Thank you, Anna!" They both smiled and Tim went home with his mom, happy and with his leg all better.

Once there was a family who lived near the forest. They were healthy and strong. Every day, the father would rush off to the forest to collect wood for their fire.
One day, the father took his 3-year-old son to the deep dark woods. The father told the son to stay still. The son was scared but he was also curious. As he watched, the father found a cave hidden in the forest. He called his son to crawl inside with him. Inside the cave, the father found a pile of gold coins, glimmering in the darkness.
The father and son were both filled with wisdom. They knew that all this wealth did not belong to them, so they rushed to put the coins back where they came from.
But, as they were leaving the cave, the ground started to shake and the cave began to crumble. The father and son were stuck inside and could not get out. All their wisdom couldn’t help them now.
The shaking stopped, the cave was filled with rubble. The father and son were buried beneath the rubble, never to be seen again.
The family mourned their loss, their healthy spirits gradually becoming sad and broken. They never found out the wisdom of the cave and the riches that lay within.

Lily and Ben wanted to fly a kite. They had a big kite with a long tail and many colors. They went to the park with their mom and dad. The park had a lot of grass and a small hill.
"Look, the wind is strong today!" Lily said. "We can make the kite go high in the sky!"
"Yes, let's go to the top of the hill!" Ben said. "We can run and let go of the kite!"
They climbed the hill with their mom and dad. They held the kite and the string. They waited for a big gust of wind.
"Ready, set, go!" Lily shouted. They ran and let go of the kite. The kite flew up and up. It looked like a bird.
"Wow, it's so beautiful!" Ben said. "Can I hold the string, Lily?"
"OK, but be careful!" Lily said. She gave the string to Ben. Ben felt the kite pull and tug. He tried to balance the kite in the air.
But the wind was rough. It made the kite shake and twist. Ben lost his grip on the string. The kite flew away.
"Oh no, our kite!" Lily cried. "We have to get it back!"
They ran after the kite. They saw it land on a big tree. The tree had many branches and leaves.
"Mom, dad, help us!" Lily and Ben said. "Our kite is stuck in the tree!"
Their mom and dad came to the tree. They looked at the kite.
"Don't worry, kids," their dad said. "I can climb the tree and get the kite. You stay here and watch."
Their dad climbed the tree. He was careful not to fall. He reached the kite and untangled it from the branches. He threw it down to the kids.
"Yay, we got our kite!" Lily and Ben said. They caught the kite and hugged it.
"Thank you, dad!" they said.
"You're welcome, kids," their dad said. He climbed down the tree and joined them.
"Let's try to fly the kite again," their mom said. "But this time, hold the string tight and work together."
"OK, mom," Lily and Ben said. They smiled and nodded. They held the kite and the string. They ran and let go of the kite. The kite flew up and up. They balanced the kite in the air. They had fun.

Lily tried to pull the pastry from the shelf, but it was too high. She tried again and again. Finally, her mom helped her. They pulled the pastry together. Lily and her mom went home and ate the pastry. They were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little train. The train loved to push carts on the track. The train was very flexible. It could bend and turn on the track easily.
One day, the train was pushing its carts on the track. It went around a big bend. Then, something unexpected happened. The train saw a big tree on the track. The train did not know what to do.
The train thought for a moment. It used its flexible body to bend around the tree. The train pushed the carts around the tree too. The train was happy it could keep going on the track. And from that day, the train knew it could face any problem on its way.

One day, a boy named Tom found a rope. The rope could glow! Tom was very happy. He played with the rope all day. He showed the rope to his friend, Sam.
"Look, Sam! My rope can glow!" Tom said.
Sam was anxious. He wanted the rope too. He thought of a plan. Sam asked Tom to play a game. The game was to see who could throw the rope the farthest. Tom agreed.
They threw the rope back and forth. Then, Sam threw the rope very, very far. Tom could not find the rope. Sam knew where the rope was, but he did not tell Tom. Tom was sad. Sam took the glowing rope for himself.

Anna and Ben are playing in the living room. They have many toys, but they are bored. They want to do something new and fun.
"Let's be creative," Anna says. "Let's make a story with the switch."
"What switch?" Ben asks.
Anna points to the light switch on the wall. "This switch. We can pretend it is magic. When we turn it on and off, different things happen in our story."
Ben likes the idea. He runs to the switch and turns it off. The room becomes dark.
"Once upon a time, there was a big dragon who lived in a cave," Anna begins. "He was very scary and mean. He liked to breathe fire and roar."
Ben turns the switch on. The room becomes bright.
"But one day, a brave knight came to the cave. He had a shiny sword and a strong shield. He wanted to stop the dragon from hurting people."
Ben turns the switch off. The room becomes dark again.
"The dragon saw the knight and was angry. He breathed fire at him and roared loudly. The knight dodged the fire and ran towards the dragon."
Ben turns the switch on. The room becomes bright again.
"The knight swung his sword and hit the dragon on the nose. The dragon cried out in pain and ran away. The knight had saved the day."
Anna and Ben clap their hands and cheer. They are happy with their story.
"That was a good story," Anna says. "You are very creative, Ben."
"Thank you, Anna. You are very creative, too. Do you want to make another story with the switch?"
"Yes, I do. Let's make a story about a princess and a frog."
They run to the switch and start their new story. They have fun being creative with the switch.

Once upon a time, there was a white cow named Mimi. Mimi lived on a big ranch with her friends. She loved to play and run in the sun. But one day, Mimi lost her favorite toy.
Mimi started to cry. Her friend, a horse named Bobo, heard her and came over. "Why are you sad, Mimi?" Bobo asked. Mimi told him about her lost toy. Bobo said, "Don't cry, Mimi. Let's look for it together."
They looked all over the ranch, but they could not find the toy. Mimi was about to cry again when a bird flew down. The bird had Mimi's toy in its beak! The bird had thought the toy was food, but when it found out it was Mimi's toy, it brought it back.
Mimi was so happy! She thanked the bird and her friend Bobo. From that day on, Mimi learned to share her toys with her friends and to be thankful for the help she got from others. And they all lived happily ever after on the big ranch.

Lily and Tom were hungry. They wanted to eat spaghetti for dinner. Mom said she would make spaghetti for them. She went to the kitchen and started to boil water.
Lily and Tom played in the living room. They had a lot of toys. They liked to pretend they were animals. Lily was a lion and Tom was a monkey. They made loud noises and jumped around.
Mom heard them and smiled. She wanted to have some fun too. She put some spaghetti on a plate and sneaked into the living room. She hid behind the couch and waited.
Lily and Tom did not see her. They kept playing. Lily roared like a lion and Tom chattered like a monkey. They ran towards the couch.
Mom jumped out and shouted, "Boo!" She held the plate of spaghetti in front of her face. She made a funny noise.
Lily and Tom were scared. They screamed and ran away. They thought Mom was a spaghetti monster.
Mom laughed and said, "It's me, it's me! I was just joking. Come here, my little animals. It's time for dinner."
Lily and Tom stopped and looked at Mom. They saw her face and the spaghetti. They realized it was a prank. They felt silly and laughed too.
They hugged Mom and said, "You scared us, Mom. But we love you. And we love spaghetti."
Mom said, "I love you too. And I'm glad you love spaghetti. Let's go to the kitchen and eat. Maybe we can have some ice cream later."
Lily and Tom were happy. They followed Mom to the kitchen. They ate spaghetti and ice cream. They had a good time. They were not scared anymore. They were glad.

Once upon a time, there was a man who liked to sell hats. He had a small shop in the town. One day, he made a very tight hat. It was so tight that no one could wear it. The man was sad because he could not sell the tight hat.
One day, dark clouds came and it started to rain. It rained so much that there was a big flood in the town. All the people were scared and did not know what to do. The man with the hat shop thought about the tight hat he could not sell.
Then, the man had an idea. He took the tight hat and put it on a hole in the ground where water was coming in. The tight hat stopped the water from coming into the town. The people were very happy and thanked the man. The man was happy too, because his tight hat saved the town from the flood.

"Hello, bald man!" Tom says.
"Hello, little boy!" the man says.
"What are you doing?" Sue asks.
"I am reading a book. It is about jets. Do you like jets?" the man says.
"Yes, we love jets!" Tom and Sue say.
"Would you like to see my book? It has pictures of jets. You can learn their names and colors." the man says.
"Yes, please!" Tom and Sue say.
The man shows them his book. They see jets of different shapes and sizes. They see jets that are red, blue, yellow, and green. They see jets that can fly high, low, fast, or slow. They learn new words like pilot, wing, engine, and tail.
"Thank you, bald man! You are very nice!" Tom and Sue say.
"You are very welcome, little ones! You are very smart!" the man says.
They give the man a hug. They put his hat on his head. They say goodbye. They run back to the park. They pretend to be jets. They make loud noises. They have fun. They are happy. They met a new friend.

The plant said, "I am not growing because I am sad. That napkin is dirty and it makes me feel bad." The little boy picked up the napkin and threw it away. The plant started to grow again! It grew bigger and stronger than ever before.
The little boy learned that keeping things clean and tidy helps everyone grow big and strong. And the plant was not lonely anymore. They were happy together, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Lola. Lola loved to adventure in the woods around her house. One day she found a wonderful jug in the woods. The jug was shimmering in the sunlight and Lola thought it was beautiful.
Lola showed the jug to her Mama and asked if she could keep it. Mama smiled and said yes, but only if Lola was honest and did not try to take anything that was not hers. Lola wanted to save the jug so she made a promise to Mama.
One day, Lola found a basket of apples near a big rock in the woods. She knew she did not own the apples and she remembered her promise to be honest. So she said to herself, “I’m going to save the jug, because being honest is important. I will leave the apples for the person who owns them.”
Lola found a special place to put the jug and it made her very happy. She smiled and thanked Mama for teaching her to stay honest.
The moral of this story is that honesty is more valuable than any treasure. Lola chose to save her jug by being true to her word.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Ben had a big truck and Lily had a doll. They were having fun until Ben saw Lily's pin. It was shiny and pink and had a flower on it. Ben wanted the pin for his truck.
"Give me your pin, Lily!" Ben said. He tried to grab the pin from Lily's hair.
"No, Ben! It's mine!" Lily said. She held the pin tight and ran away from Ben.
Ben chased Lily around the living room. He was angry and wild. He knocked over a lamp and a vase. He made a big mess.
"Stop, Ben! Stop!" Lily cried. She ran to the door and tried to open it. She wanted to go to Mommy.
But the door was locked. Mommy had locked it when she went to the kitchen. She did not want Ben and Lily to go outside.
"Help, Mommy! Help!" Lily shouted. She banged on the door with her hand.
Mommy heard Lily's voice. She came back to the living room. She saw the mess and the locked door. She saw Ben and Lily's faces. They were scared and sad.
"What happened here?" Mommy asked. She unlocked the door and hugged Lily.
"Ben wanted my pin. He was wild. He chased me. He broke things. I was scared." Lily said.
Mommy looked at Ben. He lowered his head. He felt sorry.
"Ben, why did you do that?" Mommy asked.
"I wanted the pin. It was shiny. I was mad." Ben said.
Mommy shook her head. She said, "Ben, you can't take Lily's pin. It's hers. You have to ask nicely. And you can't be wild. You have to be careful. You can't break things. You have to say sorry."
Ben nodded. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, Mommy. Can I have the pin, please?"
Lily looked at Ben. She saw his eyes. They were not angry anymore. They were sorry.
She said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. You can have the pin. But you have to be nice. And you have to share."
Ben smiled. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are nice. I will share."
Mommy smiled too. She said, "That's good, Ben. That's good, Lily. I'm proud of you. Now let's clean up the mess. And then we can have a snack."
Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "Okay, Mommy."
They helped Mommy clean up the mess. They put the toys away. They fixed the lamp and the vase. They hugged each other. They were happy. They had the pin. They had Mommy. They had each other.

One day, Sara finds a shiny thing in the kitchen. It is a teaspoon. She thinks it is very pretty and she wants to put it in her box. She takes the teaspoon and runs to her room. She opens her box and puts the teaspoon inside.
Ben sees Sara running with the teaspoon. He follows her to her room. He knocks on the door and says, "Sara, what do you have?"
Sara says, "It is a teaspoon. I found it in the kitchen. It is mine now. I put it in my box."
Ben says, "But Sara, that is not your teaspoon. That is Mom's teaspoon. She needs it to make tea. You can't take it. You have to give it back."
Sara feels nervous. She likes the teaspoon, but she does not want to make Mom angry. She does not know what to do. She looks at Ben and says, "But Ben, it is so shiny and pretty. I want to keep it. Please don't tell Mom."
Ben says, "Sara, I understand. But you can't keep things that are not yours. That is not nice. Mom will be sad if she can't find her teaspoon. And she will be mad if she knows you took it. You have to be honest and say sorry. Maybe Mom will let you have another teaspoon that you can collect."
Sara thinks for a moment. She knows Ben is right. She does not want to be mean or lie. She takes the teaspoon out of her box and says, "OK, Ben. You are a good brother. I will give the teaspoon back to Mom and say sorry. Maybe she will give me a hug and a cookie."
Ben smiles and says, "That is a good idea, Sara. I will go with you and help you. Come on, let's go."
Sara and Ben hold hands and walk to the kitchen. They find Mom and give her the teaspoon. They say sorry and hug her. Mom is not angry. She is happy that they are honest and kind. She gives them a hug and a cookie. She says, "I love you, Sara and Ben. You are good children. You can collect many things, but not my teaspoons. I have a surprise for you. I have some old teaspoons that I don't use anymore. You can have them and put them in your box. How does that sound?"
Sara and Ben are very happy. They say thank you and take the old teaspoons. They run to their room and put them in their box. They look at their things and show them to each other. They are proud of their collection. They are happy to have each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a furry pet cat named Kitty. They lived in a small house with a big red door. The door had a shiny knob that Tim liked to touch.
One day, Tim saw his friend Sam playing with a big, round ball. Tim wanted to play too. So, he went to Sam and asked, "Can I borrow your ball, please?" Sam said, "Yes, but you have to give it back tomorrow."
Tim and Kitty played with the ball all day long. They were having so much fun. But when it was time to go inside, Tim forgot to put the ball away. He went to bed and left the ball outside.
That night, a big wind came and blew the ball far, far away. The next day, Tim could not find the ball to give it back to Sam. Tim felt very sad and sorry. He learned that he should always take care of things he borrowed from his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab. The crab was very patient. He liked to play by the sea.
One day, the crab met a new friend, a small fish. The fish said, "Hi, do you want to play with me?" The crab said, "Yes, I would love to play with you."
While they were playing, the sun began to burn brightly in the sky. The crab and the fish were having so much fun that they did not notice. Soon, the crab started to feel hot. The fish said, "Let's go in the water to cool down." The patient crab agreed, and they both went into the cool water.
They played in the water all day. When the sun went down, the crab and the fish said goodbye. They promised to play together again soon. The patient crab went home, happy to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog named Tim. Tim loved to jump all day long. One day, while Tim was jumping, he saw a big rock on the ground. He thought it would be fun to jump on the rock.
Tim jumped on the rock, but it felt very uncomfortable. "Ouch!" he said. Just then, the rock started to move! "I'm not a rock, I'm a turtle!" said the turtle. Tim was so surprised!
From that day on, Tim and the turtle became best friends. They played and jumped together, and Tim learned to be more careful about what he jumped on. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a yellow kite in his toy box. He was very happy and wanted to play with it. He went outside to the park with his mom. The wind was blowing just right for flying the kite.
Tim held the kite and ran as fast as he could. The yellow kite went up in the sky. Tim's friend, Sue, saw the kite and came running over. "Wow! What a pretty kite!" Sue said. Tim was proud and called, "Thank you! Do you want to try?" Sue nodded and took the kite string.
As they played, a big gust of wind came and pulled the yellow kite away. Tim and Sue were sad. They looked and looked, but could not find the kite. Just then, an old man came over with the yellow kite. "Is this your kite?" he asked. Tim and Sue both called, "Yes!"
The old man smiled and gave them the kite. Tim and Sue said thank you and learned that it is good to share and help others. They also learned that sometimes, when you lose something, you can still find it if you keep looking and have hope.

He went to the forest and asked the animals for help. The deer said, "I know! You should eat some meat. That might help you heal." The pig said, "Great idea!"
So the pig found some delicious meat and ate it. Sure enough, the meat made him feel better. Slowly, the sore on his nose began to heal.
The pig was so happy that the meat had helped him heal. From then on, the pig ate meat whenever he was feeling down. And he was happy and tall again.

Ben and the daisy waited for the sun to come up. They talked and laughed. When the sun was up, they played all day. They were very happy. The daisy and Ben were best friends.

Sara and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and look for bugs and worms. One day, they found something unusual in the dirt. It was a small, furry animal with a long nose and tiny eyes. It was a mole.
"Look, Ben, a mole!" Sara whispered. She was afraid to scare it away.
"Wow, Sara, it's so cute!" Ben whispered back. He wanted to touch it.
They moved closer to the mole, very slowly and quietly. The mole did not see them. It was busy digging and sniffing. Sara and Ben reached out their hands and gently stroked its fur. The mole felt soft and warm.
The mole stopped digging and sniffing. It sensed something on its back. It turned around and saw Sara and Ben. It was surprised and scared. It squeaked and ran away, back into its hole.
Sara and Ben were sad. They wanted to play with the mole. They waited for it to come back, but it did not.
"Maybe it's shy," Sara said.
"Maybe it's hungry," Ben said.
They decided to leave some food for the mole near its hole. They found some bread, cheese, and carrots in the kitchen. They broke them into small pieces and put them on a plate. They carried the plate to the garden and placed it next to the mole's hole.
"Here, mole, we brought you some food," Sara whispered. "We are sorry we scared you. We just wanted to be your friends."
They hoped the mole would hear them and come out. They sat down and waited. They did not know if the mole would ever come back, but they hoped it would. They liked the mole. It was unusual and cute.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful little girl named Lily. She loved to listen and hear the sounds around her. One day, Lily was walking in the park when she saw a little bird hopping on the ground. The bird looked sad and was holding its toe.
"Little bird, why are you sad?" Lily asked. The bird looked up and said, "I hurt my toe, and I can't fly to my family in the tree." Lily thought for a moment and said, "I can help you, little bird."
Lily picked up the bird and carried it to the tree. She put the bird on a branch, and the bird's family was so happy to see it. They all sang a beautiful song that Lily could hear. Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a big hippo toy that they liked to pretend was real. They made it walk and splash and roar.
"Let's make the hippo shrink!" Ben said. He had a magic wand that he got for his birthday. He waved it at the hippo and said a silly word.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
Nothing happened. The hippo was still big and heavy.
"Maybe you need to say it louder," Lily said. She took the wand from Ben and tried again.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
Still nothing. The hippo was still big and heavy.
"Maybe the wand is broken," Ben said. He was sad. He wanted to see the hippo shrink.
"Or maybe the hippo is too big to shrink," Lily said. She had an idea. She ran inside the house and came back with a light bulb.
"Look, Ben, this is light and small. Maybe the wand can shrink this," she said. She held the light bulb in front of the hippo and waved the wand.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
The light bulb flashed and popped. It was gone. Lily and Ben gasped.
"Wow, it worked!" Ben said. He was happy. He wanted to try again.
"Let's find something else to shrink," he said. He looked around the garden and saw a flower.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
The flower wilted and fell. Lily and Ben clapped.
"Let's find something else to shrink," Lily said. She looked around the garden and saw a bird.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
The bird squeaked and flew away. Lily and Ben laughed.
"Let's find something else to shrink," Ben said. He looked around the garden and saw their dad.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
Their dad turned around and saw them. He frowned.
"What are you two doing?" he asked.
"Nothing, dad," Lily and Ben said. They hid the wand behind their backs.
"Are you sure?" their dad asked. He looked at the hippo, the light bulb, the flower and the bird. He had a feeling something was wrong.
He walked towards them and reached for the wand.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!" Lily and Ben shouted together.
Their dad blinked and felt a strange sensation. He looked down and saw that he was smaller than the hippo. He looked up and saw that Lily and Ben were bigger than him.
"Uh-oh," he said.
Lily and Ben giggled.
"Look, dad, we made you shrink!" they said.
They picked him up and hugged him.
"Don't worry, dad, we'll make you big again," they said.
They waved the wand and said another silly word.
"Biggy-wiggy-woo!"
Their dad grew back to his normal size. He was relieved.
"Thank you, kids," he said. "But please, no more shrinking. It's not safe."
"Okay, dad," Lily and Ben said. They nodded.
They put the wand away and played with the hippo.
They had fun, but they never tried to shrink anything again.

One day, they find a new car in the toy box. It is small and red, and has a button on the side. Tom picks it up and says, "Look, Sue, a new car! I wonder what it does."
He presses the button and the car makes a loud noise. "Vroom, vroom!" it says. Then it starts to move by itself. It goes forward and backward, and spins around. Tom and Sue are surprised and excited.
"Wow, this car is cool!" Sue says. "It can reverse and change gear by itself!"
They follow the car as it zooms around the room. They laugh and clap their hands. They try to catch it, but it is too fast and smart. It dodges them and goes under the table and behind the sofa.
"Come back, car, come back!" Tom and Sue shout. "We want to play with you!"
But the car does not listen. It keeps moving and making noise. It does not want to stop. It likes to be free and have fun.
Tom and Sue are sad and tired. They want the car to be their friend, not their enemy. They sit on the floor and look at each other.
"How can we make it stop?" Tom asks.
"I don't know," Sue says. "Maybe we can ask it nicely."
They decide to try. They get closer to the car and say, "Please, car, please. Can you stop and play with us? We like you and we want to share our toys with you. You are a nice car, aren't you?"
The car hears them and slows down. It stops and looks at them. It thinks for a moment. Then it says, "Beep, beep!"
Tom and Sue smile. They think the car is saying yes. They reach out and touch the car gently. The car does not move or make noise. It lets them hold it and pet it.
"Thank you, car, thank you," Tom and Sue say. "You are a good car. We are sorry we scared you. We are your friends now."
The car says, "Beep, beep!" again. It sounds happy. It likes Tom and Sue. It likes to be their friend.
They hug the car and take it to their toy box. They show it their other cars and toys. They play with it and talk to it. They have a lot of fun.
The end.

Lulu shouted with joy. And Bobo was so happy, he flew even higher, showing everyone that even a chubby bird can soar.

Sara and Ben went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many fish and shells and crabs. They also saw a jellyfish. It was big and pink and had long, long arms.
"Look, Sara, a jellyfish!" Ben said. "It looks like a balloon. Can I touch it?"
"No, Ben, don't touch it!" Sara said. "Mom said jellyfish can hurt you. They can sting you with their arms. It will make you cry and your skin will be red and sore."
"But it looks so pretty and soft," Ben said. He did not listen to Sara. He walked closer to the jellyfish. He reached out his hand to touch it.
"Ben, stop!" Sara shouted. But it was too late. The jellyfish stung Ben's hand. Ben screamed and ran back to Sara. His hand was red and swollen. He cried and cried.
Mom and Dad heard Ben's cry. They ran to him and saw his hand. They were worried and angry. They took Ben to the nurse. The nurse put some cream on his hand and wrapped it with a bandage. She told Ben to be careful and not touch jellyfish again.
"I'm sorry, Mom, Dad, Sara," Ben said. "I was silly and curious. I should have listened to Sara. She was right. Jellyfish can hurt you. I learned my lesson."
Mom, Dad, and Sara hugged Ben. They were glad he was okay. They told him they loved him and forgave him. They also told him to zip his mouth next time he wanted to do something silly and dangerous.
The moral of the story is: Listen to your elders and don't touch things that can harm you.

"No!" her mom said. "It's dangerous to be outside in the rain, it's not safe. You should stay inside."
The little girl insisted. "I want to go find worms! Just to watch them," she pleaded.
" No!" her mom said again. "Go play inside and stop insisting!"
But the little girl just smiled and ran outside, umbrella in hand. She searched the yard for worms until she saw one peeking out from the soil. She squealed with delight and started to reach for it.
Suddenly, the sky opened up and a deluge of rain came pouring down. The little girl screamed and ran back to the safety of her home.
The girl's mom had tried to warn her about the rain, but she persisted. She had been stubborn and insisted on getting her wish, and now she was safe, but a bit wet.
Most likely next time, she will remember that listening was a lot easier than insisting.

One day, a duck saw Lila's boat. The duck was ignorant. He did not know what a boat was. He thought the leaf was food and the needle was a worm. He swam to the boat and tried to eat it.
Lila saw the duck and shouted. "No, duck, no! That is my boat, not your food! The needle will hurt you!" But the duck did not listen. He bit the leaf and the needle. He felt a pain in his mouth. He quacked and spat out the boat.
Lila ran to the pond and picked up her boat. She checked the leaf and the needle. They were still okay. She was happy. She said to the duck, "You are a silly duck. You should not eat things you do not know. Next time, ask before you take." The duck was ashamed. He nodded and swam away. Lila sailed her boat again. She hoped the duck learned his lesson.

"We need to fix this wreck," one duck said.
"Let's work together to move it," said the other.
So, the ducks worked together and moved the wreck away from the pond. From that day on, they had even more fun swimming and quacking together.
The moral of the story is that two heads are better than one. Working together we can accomplish things that no one can do on their own.

Once upon a time, there was a puppy called Spot. Spot loved going for walks. One day Spot went for a walk to the park. Spot was excited to explore the park, so off he set.
He sniffed around until he came upon a branch. The branch was high up in a tree, so Spot couldn't reach it. He tried to climb up, but it was too slippery! Spot whimpered. What was he going to do?
Just then, Spot heard a voice. He looked up, and there was a friendly squirrel. Spot wagged his tail. The squirrel waved one of his paws, and pointed to a delicious looking nut that was nestled near the branch. Spot got an idea.
He jumped as high as he could, and managed to make the nut fall down from the branch. Spot was delighted! He took the nut and ran back to the park, where he enjoyed his special treat.

Once upon a time, there was a raven who liked to hop. Every day, he'd hop from tree to tree, from one side of the forest to the other.
One day, he saw a group of strange birds, who didn't hop. Curious, he flew over and spoke to them.
“What are you doing?” the raven asked.
“We’re walking, this is the normal way to move,” the birds replied.
So the raven joined them, walking alongside them, but he found it difficult and difficult to keep up.
Finally, he stopped and spoke again. “I think I like hopping better,” he said.
The birds laughed. “But hopping isn’t normal!” they said.
The raven smiled and said, “Maybe not, but just because it isn’t normal, doesn’t mean it isn’t right. We should all find our own way to do things, even if it’s different to what everyone else does.”
And so the raven returned to hopping happily through the forest, knowing that it was ok to be different.
The moral of the story is that it is ok to be different and we should be brave enough to choose our own paths, even if they go against the norm.

Once upon a time, three friends - Jack, Becky and Alfred - were walking in the park. Jack stopped in front of a big and colourful tree. "Oh wow," he marveled, "it looks so original."
Becky walked up to the tree and pulled something off it. It was a mask! "Let's eat the mask," she said.
Jack's eyes widened with shock. "No no," he said. "We shouldn't eat the mask! It might taste terrible or make us sick."
Alfred smiled. "I know what we can do instead," he said. "Let's make masks out of the tree's leaves and wear them. That would be much safer."
Becky, Jack and Alfred all agreed. So they spent the afternoon crafting the most original masks they could. When they were finished, they proudly put on their masks and danced all the way home.

Once upon a time, there was a foolish pigeon. This pigeon flew around the city looking for something to mark. Everywhere the pigeon flew, it saw something new that looked fun to mark.
One day, the pigeon flew to a park and found a beautiful statue of a bird. It was very excited and quickly began to mark the statue.
Just then, a little 3 year old child saw what the pigeon was doing and asked why it was marking the statue.
The pigeon replied that it was having fun marking everything it saw and thought the statue was beautiful.
The little child then said, "that's not a very wise thing to do. You should find things to mark that you can remove easily and that won't damage anything special like this statue."
The pigeon thanked the wise little child and made a promise to find more suitable things to mark and not to be so foolish.
The moral of this story is that it is important to think before you act and to be aware of the impact your actions may have on your surroundings.

"Mum, why do I need to wipe my hands?" asked the 3 year old, looking curiously up at his mother.
His mother smiled and said, "To keep them clean and germ-free." She then took out a rubber and handed it to him. The 3 year old took it and examined it.
"What does this do?" he asked.
"It's a special rubber for wiping your hands," replied his mother. "It'll make sure your hands are nice and clean."
The 3 year old began to rub his hands with the rubber and then smelled them. "Ugh, that's sour!" he said, scrunching up his face in distaste.
"Yes," his mother replied, "it has a bit of a sour smell, so you know it's doing its job. But don't worry, it'll go away soon."
The 3 year old nodded and continued to wipe his hands until they were completely clean.
"There," said his mother, "all done!"
The 3 year old smiled. He felt much better now that his hands were clean and germ-free.

They ran after the bird, but it flew away. They kept running until they reached a clearing. There, they saw a strange hut. It was made of sticks and leaves. It had a door, but no windows.
"Who lives here?" Lia wondered.
"Maybe the bird," Tom guessed.
They walked towards the hut, but then they heard a voice.
"Who are you? What do you want?" the voice said.
They stopped and looked around. They saw a man with a long beard and a hat. He was holding a stick. He looked angry.
"We are sorry, sir," Lia said. "We were just curious. We saw your bird and wanted to see it."
"My bird? You mean my parrot?" the man said. "He is not yours to see. He is mine. Go away!"
He waved his stick at them. Lia and Tom were scared. They turned and ran back to their hut.
"Next time, we will not follow a bird," Tom said.
"Next time, we will bring our dog," Lia said. "He will protect us."

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim went to the park. It was a wet day, and the grass was wet too. Tim saw his friend, a small bird, in a tree. The bird was trying to gather sticks to build a nest. But the sticks were wet and heavy.
"Can I help you?" Tim asked the bird. The bird nodded, and they began to gather sticks together. They found dry sticks under a big tree. They worked together to build a cozy nest for the bird.
At night, Tim went to bed and had a dream. In his dream, he was a bird too. He and his bird friend flew high in the sky. They played in the clouds and sang songs together. When Tim woke up, he smiled and knew he had a new best friend.

One day, a big dog named Max went to a lecture. He wanted to study about bones. Max sat down and listened to the teacher. The teacher was a wise, old owl. The owl talked about dry bones.
Max raised his paw and said, "I like dry bones. They are yummy!" The owl looked at Max and said, "These dry bones are not for eating. They are for learning."
Max was sad. He thought he would get to eat the dry bones. But then, something unexpected happened. A little mouse ran into the room. The mouse had a big bag of bones, just for Max! Max was very happy.
The other animals at the lecture learned that sharing is good. Max learned that studying can be fun, too. The wise, old owl smiled and said, "When we share, everyone is happy."

Once upon a time, there was a shy little plant named Pippin. Pippin lived in a big garden with many other plants. Pippin wanted to grow big and strong, but he was scared of the sun and the rain.
One day, Pippin met a wise old plant named Gramps. Gramps said, "Pippin, you must face the sun and the rain to grow. Don't be scared." Pippin listened to Gramps and tried to be brave. Slowly, Pippin started to grow.
But one day, Pippin saw a bottle of poison near the garden. Pippin was scared and didn't know what to do. He remembered Gramps' words and decided to tell the other plants. Together, they asked the gardener to take the poison away. The gardener listened and removed the poison.
Pippin learned that it was important to be brave and to help others. He grew into a big, strong plant and made many friends in the garden. The other plants were proud of Pippin and they all lived happily together.
The moral of the story is to be brave, even when you are scared, and to always help others when they need you.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play pretend. Sometimes they are pirates, sometimes they are doctors, sometimes they are teachers. Today they want to be lawyers.
They find some paper and pens. They write some rules for their game. They call them laws. They plan what to say and do. They make a court in the living room. They use pillows for chairs and a book for a gavel.
Lily is the judge. She wears a hat and glasses. Ben is the lawyer. He wears a tie and a coat. They have a case. The case is about a teddy bear. The teddy bear belongs to Lily, but Ben wants to borrow it. Lily says no, Ben says yes.
Ben is the lawyer for himself. He tells the judge why he should have the teddy bear. He says he is kind and he will take good care of it. He says he will give it back soon. He says he has no other toys to play with.
Lily is the judge and the lawyer for herself. She tells the judge why she should keep the teddy bear. She says it is hers and she loves it. She says she needs it to sleep and to hug. She says Ben has many other toys to play with.
The judge listens to both lawyers. She thinks hard. She makes a decision. She says Ben can borrow the teddy bear, but only for one hour. She says Lily can have another toy from Ben's room. She says they have to share and be nice.
Lily and Ben agree. They hug and say sorry. They swap toys and play some more. They are happy. They are good lawyers and good friends.

Mommy and Daddy were very proud of their 3 year old daughter. She had always been very obedient, never playing around when it was time to clean. This made Mommy and Daddy very happy.
One day, Daddy was singing a silly song to himself while he was cleaning the kitchen. He thought his daughter was playing in the living room, but she had snuck up on him.
"Daddy, tell me a joke!" she said.
Daddy laughed and said, "Why did the chicken go to the library?"
The daughter thought for a second before she said, "I don't know, why?"
Daddy smiled and said, "To get a book on how to cross the road!"
The daughter began to giggle and said, "That was a funny joke Daddy. I like it!"
Mommy and Daddy smiled at each other, proud of their daughter who was so obedient and still found time to enjoy jokes.

Once upon a time there was a poor cat. He lived on a lonely farm, far away from everyone. He was always so lonely and wished he had someone to talk to. One day, the cat got an amazing idea – he would build a network of friends. He bounded around the farm, talking to all the animals he met, inviting them to be his friends.
"Let's be friends!", he meowed.
One by one, the animals replied with a wary yes. The cat was so happy – he finally had a network of friends! But soon, the cat realised that he had made a mistake. All the animals were too busy with their own things to pay attention to the cat, leaving him feeling lonelier than ever before.
The moral of this story is that having a network of friends is not always the answer. Quality relationships matter more than just having many friends.

Lily said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was curious. I wanted to see what was in the box."
Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm not mad. I was curious too when I was your age. Do you want to see what's in the box with me?"
Lily nodded. She was happy. Her mom said, "This box has some old stuff from my grandma. She gave it to me before she went to heaven. She loved you very much. She wanted you to have some of her stuff too."
Lily and her mom opened the box together. They found some books, some dolls, some jewelry, and some pictures. Her mom told her stories about her grandma and how she used to play with the same stuff. She encouraged Lily to ask questions and touch the stuff. Lily felt close to her mom and her grandma. She learned a lot of new things. She was glad she was curious.

Suddenly, Tim started to shrink! He got smaller and smaller until he was as tiny as a bug. Tim was scared, but then he saw a little door that he could fit through now. He went through the door and found a tiny world with tiny people just like him.
Tim played with the tiny people and had lots of fun. But then, he remembered his big family and wanted to go back. One of the tiny people told him to push the button on the tube again. Lily and Ben were playing with paper and scissors. They liked to cut shapes and make animals and flowers. Lily cut a big circle and said, "Look, Ben, I made a sun!"
Ben looked at her paper and said, "That's not a sun, Lily. That's a ball. A sun has rays and is yellow. Your paper is white."
Lily felt sad and said, "No, Ben, it's a sun. I can make it yellow with crayons. And I can draw rays too. You are ignorant, Ben. You don't know anything."
Ben felt angry and said, "I'm not ignorant, Lily. You are ignorant. You don't know how to cut properly. Your circle is not even. And your scissors are dull. You need new scissors."
Lily and Ben started to argue and shout. They did not listen to each other. They did not answer each other's questions. They only said mean things.
Mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the paper and scissors on the floor and the crayons on the table. She saw Lily and Ben with red faces and tears in their eyes. She said, "Lily and Ben, what are you doing? Why are you fighting?"
Lily and Ben stopped arguing and looked at Mom. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We were playing with paper and scissors, but we disagreed on what we made. We said ignorant things to each other. We didn't answer nicely. We didn't share."
Mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you're sorry, Lily and Ben. It's okay to have different ideas and opinions, but it's not okay to be rude and hurtful. You should respect each other and listen to each other. You should answer politely and kindly. You should share your paper and scissors and crayons. Do you understand?"
Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, Mom, we understand. We're sorry. Can we hug and make up?"
Mom said, "Of course, you can. I love you both. Now, why don't you show me your paper and scissors creations? I'm sure they're beautiful and creative."

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big melon growing on a vine. It was green and round and shiny. Anna and Ben both wanted to pick the melon and eat it.
"I saw it first!" Anna said. "It is mine!"
"No, I saw it first!" Ben said. "It is mine!"
They started to pull the melon from different sides. They pulled and pulled, but the melon did not come off. They pulled harder and harder, but the melon still did not come off. They pulled so hard that they fell down on the ground.
Then they heard a loud noise. They looked up and saw a big bird flying over them. It had a wide beak and sharp claws. It saw the melon and wanted to eat it too. It swooped down and grabbed the melon with its beak. It flew away with the melon, leaving Anna and Ben with nothing.
Anna and Ben felt sad and angry. They had lost the melon because they were greedy and selfish. They realized that they should have shared the melon and enjoyed it together. They also realized that they should have been careful of the bird, who was watching them from the sky.
They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sharing is caring, and that greed can lead to trouble. They also learned to be aware of their surroundings, and to look out for each other. They hugged and said sorry to each other. They decided to be better friends and to find another melon to share.

Lily and Tom were playing hide and seek in the old house. Lily was the seeker and Tom was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then opened her eyes. She looked around the dusty rooms, but she could not see Tom. She called out, "Tom, where are you? I miss you!"
Tom heard Lily's voice, but he did not answer. He had found a good hiding spot under the stairs. He was behind a big cobweb that made him look like a ghost. He thought it was funny and he wanted to scare Lily. He waited for her to come closer.
Lily walked through the hall, looking for Tom. She saw a door that was slightly open. She pushed it and entered a dark room. She felt anxious. She did not like the dark. She wished Tom was with her. She said, "Tom, are you here? Please come out!"
Tom heard Lily enter the room. He decided to surprise her. He ran out of his hiding spot and shouted, "Boo!" He waved his arms and made a scary face.
Lily screamed and jumped back. She saw Tom covered in cobweb and she thought he was a monster. She was very scared and she started to cry.
Tom realized he had made a mistake. He saw Lily crying and he felt sorry. He ran to her and hugged her. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was only joking. I'm not a monster. I'm your brother. Don't cry. I love you."
Lily stopped crying and hugged Tom back. She said, "I love you too, Tom. But don't do that again. You scared me a lot. And you look silly with all that cobweb on you."
Tom laughed and said, "You're right. I look silly. Let's go and wash it off. And then we can play something else. Maybe we can make a cake with mom."
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, let's do that. That sounds fun. And yummy."
They held hands and left the old house. They were happy to be together. They did not miss the cobweb or the dark. They only missed the cake.

The squirrel looked at all of the kids and whistled to them. The kids jumped with excitement, and the squirrel hopped down from the tree. The kids said, "Hi squirrel! What's your name?"
The squirrel smiled and whistled at them. He pointed to his chest, and the kids could just make out the word 'Nutty' in his deep, gentle whistle. The kids laughed, excited to have a new friend called Nutty.
They all spent the afternoon playing together in the park, and Nutty the squirrel got to join the group. The kids waved goodbye to Nutty as he ran up the tree, and they went home with big smiles, happy to have made a new friend.

"Oh, what a nice frame," she said. "I wonder where it came from. I think I'll hang it on the wall."

"How did we shrink?" Lily asked. "We need to get out!"
