Anna likes to play with her spinning top. She spins it on the floor and watches it go round and round. She likes the colors and the sound it makes. She thinks it is fun and pretty.
One day, Anna goes to the park with her mom and dad. She brings her top with her in her backpack. She plays on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. She has a lot of fun with the other kids. She forgets about her top.
When it is time to go home, Anna puts on her backpack and follows her mom and dad. They walk to the car and get in. Anna feels something hard in her backpack. She opens it and sees her top. She is happy and wants to spin it.
But her mom says no. She says it is not a good place to play with the top. She says it might roll away or hit someone. She says Anna has to wait until they get home. Anna is frustrated. She does not want to wait. She wants to play with her top now.
She tries to sneak it out of her backpack. But her dad sees her. He says no too. He says Anna has to listen to her mom. He says they will be home soon. Anna is more frustrated. She does not like to listen. She thinks it is not fair.
She puts her top back in her backpack. She crosses her arms and pouts. She looks out the window and sighs. She hopes they get home soon. She wants to spin her top. She thinks it is the best toy ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little raft. It was upset because it could not number how many friends it had. One day, the raft met a big fish. The fish said, "Hi, raft! I can help you number your friends."
The raft was happy. It said, "Thank you, fish!" The fish helped the raft number its friends. They counted one, two, three friends. But then, something unexpected happened.
A big wave came and pushed the raft away from its friends. The raft was upset again. But the big fish had an idea. The fish called all the raft's friends, and they worked together to bring the raft back. The raft was happy again, and it thanked the big fish and its friends for their help.

Emily was a little girl and she wanted to do her best. She went to school and the teacher pointed at her and said she had to take a test. Emily was a bit scared but she did her best. When the test was over, she felt ashamed because she made some mistakes.
The teacher said to Emily that she did her best and gave her a big hug. Emily felt better and she was so happy.
The teacher said that in life you have to try your best and sometimes mistakes happen. Emily was smiling again and full of hope. She knew that if she kept trying, she could do better next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Clara. She wanted to record something special every day. One day, she decided to take out her recorder and record a yummy bowl of ice-cream she just served herself.
Clara: "Yummy yummy! I love ice-cream!"
As she was eating her ice-cream, she thought to herself how useful recorders were to record special moments. She decided to record herself every single day.
Now, Clara has a collection of recordings full of special moments. Whenever she plays them back, she smiles, because the recorder has been so useful to her.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a red ball that he loved to play with. One day, he went to the park to play with his red ball. While playing, he saw a big tree with a key hanging from one of its branches. Tim was very curious about the key.
Tim asked his friend, Sally, "Do you see the key in the tree?" Sally looked up and said, "Yes, I see it! I wonder what it is for." Tim and Sally decided to watch the key to see if anything would happen. They sat under the tree and watched the key for a long time.
As they watched, a little bird flew down and picked up the key in its beak. Tim and Sally were so excited! They followed the bird to a small house. The bird used the key to open the door, and inside was a big pile of shiny, red apples. The bird shared the apples with Tim and Sally, and they all had a fun time eating the apples and playing together.

One day, a baby was playing with his toy. He felt very important because it was his favorite toy. He was so happy and laughed a lot.
But then, a big boy came and took the toy away. The baby was very sad and started to scream. The big boy did not care and just walked away.
The baby's mommy heard the scream and came running. She saw the big boy and said, "Give the toy back, it is important to the baby." The big boy gave the toy back and said, "I am sorry." The baby stopped screaming and started to laugh again. They all played together and had a fun day.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the garden. She saw a wet onion in the dirt. Lily gazed at the onion and picked it up. She wanted to show her mom the big wet onion she found.
Lily went inside and showed her mom the onion. Her mom smiled and said, "Let's cut the onion and see what's inside." They went to the kitchen and cut the onion. Inside the onion, they found a shiny key!
Lily and her mom were very surprised. They looked all around the house to find what the key opened. Finally, they found a little box in the attic. Lily used the key to open the box. Inside, they found a pretty necklace that belonged to her grandma. Lily and her mom were so happy to find the special necklace from the wet onion.

Once upon a time, there was a furry clown. He had a big red nose and a polka dot bow tie. The clown liked to wrap too. He would wrap presents for all the children.
One day, the furry clown was walking in the park when he saw a little girl. He called out to her, "Hello, little girl! Do you want a present?"
The little girl looked up at the clown and smiled. "Yes," she said. "I would love a present!"
The furry clown smiled back. He reached into his sack and pulled out a present. He carefully wrapped it up with pretty paper and ribbons. The little girl thanked him with a hug and ran off to show her mommy.
The furry clown smiled and watched her go. Wrapping presents was the best part of being a clown!

Once upon a time, there was a modest jeep. It was not too big, and not too small. The jeep had four wheels and liked to drive around. One day, the jeep met a little boy named Tim.
"Hi jeep! Can I ride with you?" Tim asked. The jeep was happy and let Tim ride with it. They went up and down the hills, and around the trees. Tim laughed and had fun.
As they drove, Tim saw his friends. He waved to them and said, "Look at my jeep! It's the best!" His friends clapped and cheered. They all wanted to ride with Tim and the modest jeep. The jeep felt proud and happy, and they all had a great day together.

One day, a little girl named Lucy found a lucky coin on the floor. She was very happy and showed it to her friend, Tom. "Look, Tom! I found a lucky coin!" said Lucy. Tom was very excited too.
Lucy and Tom wanted to prevent anyone from taking their lucky coin. So, they decided to hide it behind the curtain in Lucy's room. They knew it would be safe there.
Later, Lucy's mom came into the room and saw the curtain moving. "What's behind the curtain?" she asked. Lucy and Tom looked at each other and smiled. "It's our lucky coin!" they said. Lucy's mom smiled too and knew their secret was safe.

Once upon a time, there was a cat. The cat loved to paint. One day, the cat found a big, heavy rock. The cat wanted to paint the rock.
The cat tried to move the heavy rock. But it was too heavy. The cat was sad. The cat wanted help to move the rock. The cat asked a dog for help. The dog said, "No, I will not help you."
The cat was sad but did not give up. The cat asked a bird for help. The bird said, "Yes, I will help you." The bird and the cat moved the heavy rock together. The cat was happy.
The cat painted the rock with the bird. They painted it with many colors. The cat and the bird were happy. They made a pretty rock. They were friends.

Once there was a family who lived in a big house. The house had a very special unlockable door which the family kept secret. No one knew what was behind the door.
One day, the family went out and left their three-year-old daughter alone at home. The daughter was curious and wondered what was behind the mysterious door.
She found an old key and tried to unlock the door. Much to her surprise, it opened. Inside, she discovered lots of thoughtful presents, which her family had secretly been saving for her special occasions. She was so excited by the discovery, she couldn't help but laugh.
The family had been so thoughtful and kind to put together such a thoughtful collection of presents, filled with so much value. The young girl was so thankful for her family and understood the value of their generous gift. From then on, she kept the door unlocked, so she could always remember the thoughtful presents that her family had given her.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Bobo. Bobo had a long chain that he did not like. He thought it was a stupid chain because it was too big for him. So, he asked his friend, a wise old cat named Whiskers, what he should do.
Whiskers thought for a moment and then said, "I recommend you find a smaller chain that fits you better." Bobo liked this idea and went to look for a new chain.
Bobo found a small chain that was perfect for him. He was very happy and thanked Whiskers for his help. Now, Bobo and Whiskers play together every day, and Bobo never has to worry about his stupid chain again.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet puppy named Spot. Spot loved to play at the park with his friends. Every day, he would run and jump with joy.
One sunny day, Spot went to the park with his owner, a little girl named Lily. They played fetch with a ball. Spot was very fast and always brought the ball back to Lily. They were both very happy.
As the sun began to set, it was time to go home. Spot and Lily said goodbye to their friends at the park. They walked home together, looking forward to another fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play in his yard. One day, Spot saw a big red ball near the gate. He wanted to play with the ball.
Spot ran to the gate and tried to open it. He used his nose to push, but the gate did not open. Spot tried to snap the gate with his teeth, but it still did not open. He was sad.
Then, Spot's friend, a small cat named Whiskers, came to help. Whiskers jumped on the gate and opened it with her paw. Spot was so happy! They played with the big red ball all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a big coat that she loved to wear. The coat was warm and soft, but sometimes it felt harsh when the wind blew hard.
One day, Lucy went for a walk with her mom. She wore her big coat because it was cold outside. As they walked, they saw a little kitten shivering in the cold. Lucy felt sad for the kitten.
Lucy picked up the kitten and gave it a big kiss. She put the kitten inside her coat to keep it warm. The kitten was so happy and snuggled close to Lucy. From that day on, Lucy and the kitten were the best of friends.

Sara and Ben are playing in the garden. They have a big box of toys. Sara likes to bury her toys in the sand. She thinks it is fun to dig them out later. Ben likes to keep his toys tidy. He puts them in the box when he is done.
"Look, Sara, I buried my doll!" Sara says. She shows Ben a hole in the sand. "Can you find her?"
"No, Sara, I don't want to play that game. It is messy. You will lose your toys. And the sand will get in their eyes and hair. It is not nice." Ben says. He shakes his head.
"But it is fun, Ben. And I can always find them. See?" Sara says. She digs out her doll. She brushes off the sand. "She is fine. She likes to hide."
"Sara, stop it. You are making the garden dirty. And you are ruining your toys. They will get old and broken. You should be more careful." Ben says. He frowns. He picks up his car. He puts it in the box.
Sara and Ben start to argue. They raise their voices. They do not listen to each other. They are not happy.
Mama hears them. She comes out of the house. She sees the sand and the toys. She sees Sara and Ben. She is not happy either.
"Sara, Ben, what are you doing? Why are you fighting? And why is the garden so messy?" Mama says. She looks at them. She is angry.
Sara and Ben stop arguing. They look at Mama. They are scared.
"Mama, we are sorry. We were playing. But we like different games. Sara likes to bury her toys. I like to keep them tidy. We could not agree." Ben says.
"Yes, Mama, we are sorry. We were having fun. But Ben does not like my game. He thinks it is bad. He does not understand." Sara says.
Mama sighs. She kneels down. She hugs them.
"Sara, Ben, I love you both. But you need to learn to respect each other. And to respect your toys. And to respect the garden. It is not nice to bury your toys. It is not nice to make a mess. It is not nice to fight. You should be more gentle. And more tidy. And more kind." Mama says.
Sara and Ben nod. They feel sorry. They want to make Mama happy.
"Mama, we will be more gentle. And more tidy. And more kind. We will not bury our toys. We will not make a mess. We will not fight. We will play nicely." Sara and Ben say.
Mama smiles. She kisses them.
"That's good, Sara and Ben. I am glad you understand. Now, let's clean up the garden. And then we can have a snack. And then we can play something else. Something that you both like. How about that?" Mama says.
Sara and Ben smile. They like that idea. They help Mama clean up the sand and the toys. They put them in the box. They make the garden tidy. They are proud of their work. They have a good view of the flowers and the birds. They are happy.
They go inside with Mama. They have a snack. They thank Mama. They hug Mama. They love Mama.
They play something else. Something that they both like. They share their toys. They take turns. They laugh. They have fun.
They are friends.
